documents.unit: Artificial Intelligence at PCC (college AI site)
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence at PCC
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule itself: 'Expectations for AI use in a course are determined by the instructor' and 'PCC does not yet have any specific Artificial Intelligence policy', so the decision is delegated to instructors.
documents.summary: College-wide AI landing page. It says PCC welcomes AI where it advances the mission, has no dedicated AI policy yet, and leaves course expectations to instructors, with board policies as interim guidance.

units.why: The opening sentence sets the college's institutional stance: PCC 'embraces emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI)', but only 'to the extent that they advance this mission'. That is a framework statement for all of PCC (all, general, informs), so P56; it welcomes AI conditionally, hence permit.
units.anchor: PCC embraces emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), to the extent that they advance

units.why: States a principle: AI 'may enhance teaching and learning, but it must do so in ways that center students, uphold equity, and respect the professional judgment of faculty.' It is a principle for the whole institution (P56); P51 would be too narrow because equity is only one of three conditions.
units.anchor: center students, uphold equity, and respect the professional judgment of faculty
units.frag_start: AI may enhance teaching and learning

units.why: 'Expectations for AI use in a course are determined by the instructor and may differ from class to class' hands the decision to each instructor, so P04. It informs students (actor student, course-start) and sets no rule of its own.
units.anchor: Expectations for AI use in a course are determined by the instructor

units.why: 'Check your syllabus and talk to your instructor' tells students to find out the rule before acting, which is P10. It is a recommendation, so should. P04 is the previous unit; this sentence is the student action.
units.anchor: Check your syllabus and talk to your instructor.

units.why: 'PCC supports faculty in integrating AI into their teaching thoughtfully and on their own terms' with consultations offered is faculty support, P63. 'On their own terms' also confirms instructor discretion, but the main act is support.
units.anchor: PCC supports faculty in integrating AI into their teaching thoughtfully and on their own terms.

units.why: 'PCC does not yet have any specific Artificial Intelligence policy' but existing board-approved policies (academic integrity, conduct, IT use, privacy) 'offer immediate interim guidance'. This makes existing policy govern AI use, so P77. The word 'yet' hints at P54 but promises no revision, so P77 is the better fit.
units.anchor: PCC does not yet have any specific Artificial Intelligence policy
units.fit_note: Also signals that a dedicated AI policy does not yet exist (the word 'yet'), which P77 does not capture.

documents.unit: Artificial Intelligence at PCC (college AI site)
documents.title: Student learning and AI
documents.stance_why: The page defers to instructors ('determined by the instructor and may differ from class to class') and adds only a citation conduct rule, with no tiers or college-wide default, so delegates.
documents.summary: Student-facing page. Instructors set course rules; uncited AI text violates the Student Code of Conduct. It lists vetted tools, resources and routes to appeal or complain.

units.why: Repeats on the student page that 'Expectations for AI use in a course are determined by the instructor', a delegation of the rule to instructors (P04). No college-wide rule is set here.
units.anchor: Expectations for AI use in a course are determined by the instructor

units.why: 'Check your syllabus and talk to your instructor' tells students where to learn the rule, P10; should because it is advice.
units.anchor: Check your syllabus and talk to your instructor.

units.why: 'Using AI-generated text without citation is a violation under Article IV of the Student Code of Conduct.' Failing to cite is itself the violation, so P28 (nondisclosure as violation) rather than P36 (unauthorized use generally); it also implies a citation duty. Binds students, when-misuse, must-not.
units.anchor: Using AI-generated text without citation is a violation under Article IV

units.why: 'Citing generative AI: Library guidance on citing AI-generated content' points students to library citation guidance. It supports the citation duty (P24) but only names a resource, so it informs and the fit is partial.
units.anchor: Library guidance on citing AI-generated content.
units.fit_note: Only points to library citation guidance; it states no citation requirement itself.

units.why: 'Always consider how to protect your data when using AI applications' is advice to students on data protection, P50. 'Always consider' is a recommendation, hence should.
units.anchor: Always consider how to protect your data when using AI applications.

units.why: 'PCC-provided tools have been vetted by the PCC Information Security team' presents institution-vetted tools as safer, the 'prefer vetted tools' part of P50. It is a fact statement (informs).
units.anchor: PCC-provided tools have been vetted by the PCC Information Security team.

units.why: 'In PCC-provided tools, your content is not used to train any models, and you retain ownership of your materials' states data-use and ownership terms for the provided tools, which fits P52 (ownership of AI inputs and outputs). Informs only.
units.anchor: your content is not used to train any models, and you retain ownership
units.fit_note: Also a privacy assurance (no model training), which P52 does not name.

units.why: Lists 'Google Gemini' and 'Gemini Notebook' under the security text about 'PCC-provided tools', so the college supplies sanctioned AI tools, P17. The list is a statement of fact that makes them available.
units.fit_note: Only names the tools; does not say whether any course must use them.

units.why: 'AI literacy: Understanding what AI is, how it works, and its limitations' offers AI-literacy resources to students, P70.
units.anchor: Understanding what AI is, how it works, and its limitations.

units.why: 'AI ethical considerations: Ethical considerations for using Artificial Intelligence' points to an ethics resource, P53; it only names a resource and gives no content, so the fit is partial.
units.anchor: Ethical considerations for using Artificial Intelligence.
units.fit_note: Names a resource page without stating specific harms.

units.why: Directs students with questions about responsible use, citing or deciding whether AI fits an assignment to 'a faculty librarian in person' or a research help appointment: human help alongside AI, P72.
units.anchor: Contact a faculty librarian in person at the library
units.frag_start: Contact a faculty librarian in person

units.why: 'What if my use of AI impacted my grade? Speak with your instructor or use the grade appeal process' gives students a route to contest AI-related grade outcomes: right to respond, P64.
units.anchor: Speak with your instructor or use the

units.why: 'What if I have been unfairly accused or treated regarding my use of AI? ... use the formal complaint process' gives accused students a way to respond, P64.
units.anchor: unfairly accused or treated regarding my use of AI

notes: No computing, school or course documents were collected. Linked board policies were not followed.
